McLaren.summary: McLaren has added a tiny winglet to the front brake ducts, shaping the airflow right at the front corners of the car. The tweak cleans up turbulent air, giving the brakes better cooling and generating a bit more front‑end grip, which should translate into quicker turn‑ins and more stable handling on this weekend’s circuit. In short, the car will feel tighter through the twists, giving McLaren a better chance to fight for the podium.

Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari has given the car a fresh set of “aerodynamic tweaks” – reshaping the front floor, extending the edge wing and re‑profiling the floor fences to smooth the airflow under the car, and enlarging the diffuser at the rear. A modest update to the rear‑wing pillar winglet adds a little extra bite, helping the car stay planted in fast corners. Together these changes should boost grip and stability, letting the drivers push harder through the bends and manage tyre wear more effectively this weekend.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull has fitted a slightly longer flap on the front wing, giving the car a bit more bite up front and helping it stay glued to the road through the high‑speed corners this weekend. At the same time, the cooling louvers have been widened, letting more air flow through the sidepods so the power unit stays in its optimal temperature window and can deliver maximum performance on the straights. In short, better front‑end grip and more reliable engine cooling should translate into stronger lap times and a more consistent drive around the circuit.

Haas F1 Team.summary: Haas has tweaked the rear of the car by opening up the central part of the engine cover, giving the power unit a bigger “breathing” slot that's tailored to this weekend’s circuit. The extra airflow helps keep temperatures down, meaning the engine can stay in its optimal window longer and the drivers can push harder without worrying about overheating. In short, it’s a simple‑look change that could translate into more consistent lap times and a better chance at scoring points.
